decision.summaryForCoordinator: This artifact is pure quotation, so the review was pure equality testing: one top-level list plus id, memberVerbatim, exactByteIntent and passProperty for each of two classes — nine checks, nine equal. I indexed the live classes by memberVerbatim rather than by position, so a mis-pairing between the two classes would have surfaced rather than passing silently, and the class ids match live as well, meaning identity, member text, intent and pass property all travel together. The two exactByteIntent strings are several hundred characters each and are carried whole with no truncation and no altered punctuation, which is worth stating plainly because truncated or altered quotation has been the recurring defect class this session and produced findings in the FX-5, FX-6 and FX-10 chains. One thing deserves flagging so a later mechanical check does not misfire. Four prohibited terms — PURGED, D9 code, exit number, purge recipe — do appear in this artifact, and all four appear because live G19's own exactByteIntent contains the sentence 'they do not author a purge recipe, D9 code, exit number, or PURGED typed result'. They are G19's refusals, carried inside a field I verified byte-equal to live. A token sweep would flag this artifact; the correct test is whether the containing field equals live, and it does. Everything invented is nothing: both classes carry fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED, both quoted intents end with G19's own 'Fixtures are unauthored', the bare-integer set is only 0, 04, 08, 1 and 26, and no envelope, structure or result shape is defined. Coherence with the adjacent leftover-join is exact: that join's OBL-G19-FX-AUTHORING is still leftoverDesign true with an identical two-class list, and this catalog explicitly does not close it. Naming a leftover in more detail is precisely the move that could read as progress on it, and this pair keeps the measurement and the detail separate.
